features: Open with the instrument and current market state.
Use explicit if-then conditions instead of unconditional prediction.
Name the next level or observation that would confirm or invalidate the view.
Keep background explanation secondary to the immediate market read.
Lead with one quantified observation when that is the whole useful update.
Do not pad a single-data update into an essay.
Let a chart or linked source carry detail when available.
Start with the event and the size of the move.
Separate reported drivers from the writer's own interpretation.
Add cross-asset or positioning context only when it changes the read.
Finish with the concrete level or signal the market is watching next.
Define an unfamiliar metric before interpreting it.
Use one chart or metric as the organizing object rather than stacking unrelated facts.
Move from definition to present reading to bounded interpretation.
Use a debatable question or thesis as the title.
Define the model or heuristic before evaluating it.
Organize evidence into a small number of distinct forces rather than a chronology dump.
Include counter-risks and limits before implications.
End with what the reader should monitor, not a certainty claim.
